record.paper_title: Trimer Covers in the Triangular Grid: Twenty Mostly Open Problems
record.original_question: Let T(n) = T112(3n+1, 3n+2), where T112(a,b) counts tilings of the (a,b)-benzel when both stone orientations are allowed and exactly two of the three bone orientations are allowed. Is it true that for every n >= 1 the quotient T(n) T(n+3) / (T(n+1) T(n+2)) equals 65536(2n+3)(2n+5)^2(2n+7)(4n+3)(4n+5)^2(4n+7)^2(4n+9)^2(4n+11) / (729(3n+2)(3n+4)^3(3n+5)^2(3n+7)^2(3n+8)^3(3n+10))?

evidence.quote: For 0 <= i, j <= 1 and 0 <= k <= 3 we define Tijk (a, b) as the number of ways to tile the (a, b)-benzel if the set of allowed prototiles contains the right stone iff i = 1, contains the left stone iff j = 1, and contains k of the bones. We say that such a tiling is an i, j, k tiling.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For integers $a, b \geq 0$, consider the $(a,b)$-benzel: a hexagonal-shaped region in the triangular lattice (a finite subregion of the triangular grid obtained by removing certain triangular corners from a hexagonal region parameterized by $a$ and $b$). The allowed prototiles consist of two kinds of "stones" (the right stone and the left stone, two distinct trimer shapes that are rotations of each other) and three kinds of "bones" (three trimer shapes corresponding to the three orientations of a straight tromino on the triangular grid). For $i,j \in \{0,1\}$ and $k \in \{0,1,2,3\}$, let $T_{ijk}(a,b)$ denote the number of tilings of the $(a,b)$-benzel using prototiles drawn from the set that includes the right stone iff $i=1$, the left stone iff $j=1$, and exactly $k$ of the three bone orientations (with a fixed choice of which $k$ orientations are allowed when ambiguity arises).

Define $T(n) = T_{112}(3n+1,\, 3n+2)$, the number of tilings of the $(3n+1,3n+2)$-benzel in which both stone orientations and exactly two of the three bone orientations are permitted.

Prove or disprove: for every integer $n \geq 1$,
$$\frac{T(n)\, T(n+3)}{T(n+1)\, T(n+2)} \;=\; \frac{65536\,(2n+3)(2n+5)^2(2n+7)(4n+3)(4n+5)^2(4n+7)^2(4n+9)^2(4n+11)}{729\,(3n+2)(3n+4)^3(3n+5)^2(3n+7)^2(3n+8)^3(3n+10)}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: According to Jim Propp's benzel tilings status page, Problem 10 is listed as solved, attributed to work by Byun, Ciucu, and Lee ("Solution of some tiling open problems of Propp, Lai, and some related results"). Related work using generalized compression methods has resolved several of the original twenty conjectures.

status_evidence.title: Tilings of benzels via generalized compression
status_evidence.snippet: compression techniques convert problems involving 3-cell tiles to those involving 2-cell tiles, resolving several Propp benzel conjectures
status_evidence.claim: Several of Propp's benzel conjectures have been resolved via compression methods.
